entries.title: Psalms 94:1
segments:
. The writer, appealing to God in view of the oppression of enemies, rebukes them for their wickedness and folly, and encourages himself, in the confidence that God will punish evildoers, and favor His people. 
 
    1, 2. God's revenge is His judicial infliction of righteous punishment. 
 
    show thyself--(Compare Margin).

entries.title: Psalms 94:3
segments: 3, 4. In an earnest expostulation he expresses his desire that the insolent triumph of the wicked may be ended.

entries.title: Psalms 94:9
segments: 9-11. The evidence of God's providential government is found in His creative power and omniscience, which also assure us that He can punish the wicked in regard to all their vain purposes.

entries.title: Psalms 94:12
segments: 12, 13. On the other hand He favors though He chastens, the pious, and will teach and preserve them till the prosperous wicked are overthrown.
